regions.summary: Rural and western Anyang: Anyang county, Yindu and Long'an districts, plus Linzhang across the Zhang River in Hebei.
regions.notes: The label 'yin du' sits on this region. Yindu is the Yin ruins district; 'anyang' is on the small city region 2.

regions.summary: Anyang city centre: Wenfeng and Beiguan districts (old Zhangde prefecture city).
regions.notes: Small region with the 'anyang' label drawn over it.

regions.summary: Linzhou (old Linlu, Lin county) in the Taihang foothills, plus a slice of Hebi's hills.
Qingfeng county and the Neihuang part east of the Wei River.
Tangyin county with the Hebi hill districts Shancheng and Heshan.
Puyang city centre (Hualong district, old Kaizhou).
regions.notes: No label sits exactly on this tiny region; 'pu yang' is drawn just to its left, on region 9's edge, so I read it as region 6's label spilling over. Region 9's own label is 'dao kou' just below. If 'pu yang' is meant for region 9, then 6 is unnamed and Kaizhou or Hualong would fit.

regions.summary: Fan county and the eastern half of Puyang county, down to the Yellow River bank.
Hebi city core and the Qi River valley: Qi county, Qibin district and the western half of Jun county.

candidates.name: Zhaoge
candidates.meaning: "Morning song": the late Shang dynasty's secondary capital and the Zhou-era Wei capital, at today's Qi county.
candidates.fit: Seat of Zhaoge county (221 BC-605) and Zhaoge commandery at Qi; the region holds all of Qi county (32% of people), most of Qibin and half of Jun.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 381 hits with Henan, top ones about Qi county and Hebi; also the setting of the Fengshen story.
candidates.source_note: 朝歌，商朝晚期的国都。一般认为位于河南省淇县县城内

candidates.name: Hebi
candidates.meaning: "Crane wall": from a cliff where cranes were said to nest, named for the old market town Hebiji.
candidates.fit: Hebi's urban seat Qibin lies here (68% of Qibin), though Heshan and Shancheng, the old Hebi town, are in region 5.
candidates.recognisability: Current prefecture-level city, 1.57M people; always known.
candidates.source_note: prefecture seat Qibin district

regions.summary: Hua county (Daokou), the south of Neihuang and Puyang county, Hualong's outskirts.
regions.notes: See region 6: two labels ('pu yang', 'dao kou') fall inside this region's outline.

regions.summary: Huixian city and the north edge of Weihui, below the Taihang.
Xinxiang city: Weibin, Hongqi, Muye parts and Xinxiang county.

candidates.name: Xinxiang
candidates.meaning: "New village": from the Han township Xinzhong ("new middle") in Ji county, shortened to Xinxiang in the Sui.
candidates.fit: Holds all of Weibin, the old centre, and most of Xinxiang county and Hongqi; the city's other regions need other names.
candidates.recognisability: Current city and county; always known.
candidates.source_note: 以汲县新中乡简称新乡得名

regions.notes: Xinxiang's urban area is split between this region and region 15, which also holds Hongqi, Muye and Fengquan parts.

regions.summary: Jiaozuo city: Shanyang, Jiefang, Macun and most of Xiuwu county.

candidates.name: Jiaozuo
candidates.meaning: Either a kiln-owning Jiao family, or "jiao zao" (scorched jujube) in memory of Shanxi settlers who ate jujubes here.
candidates.fit: Holds the three urban districts Shanyang, Jiefang and Macun, the Jiaozuo coal city; city name goes to the central region.
candidates.recognisability: Current city; always known.
candidates.source_note: 名称渊源

candidates.name: Xiuwu
candidates.meaning: "Repair arms": traditionally King Wu of Zhou readying his troops here before the Shang campaign (not checked); a county name since the Qin and Han.
candidates.fit: County makes 20% of the region's people (83% of the county) and 44% of its area; Yuntai Mountain is in it.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, many hits; known for Yuntai Mountain.
candidates.source_note: 修武是孔子問禮之地、漢獻帝謫居之地、“竹林七賢”隱居之地

regions.notes: Meaning for Xiuwu is the commonly given explanation; not checked against a source in the batch.

regions.summary: Changyuan city (Zhangyuan in facts.json is a romanisation slip) beside the Yellow River.

candidates.name: Changyuan
candidates.meaning: "Long wall": a Qin county named for a long wall or rampart in the Wey/Wei state area.
candidates.fit: 88% of the region's people live in Changyuan, which is 98% inside the region; the rest is a sliver of Fengqiu.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city (formerly Changyuan county), 2000+ years old.
candidates.source_note: 秦朝始置长垣县，此为长垣得名之始

regions.notes: facts.json spells the county 'Zhangyuan'. 长垣 is read Changyuan in Mandarin.

regions.summary: Huaiqing seat: Qinyang city, Bo'ai county, Zhongzhan and part of Shanyang.

candidates.name: Huaiqing
candidates.meaning: "Celebrating Huai": Ming and Qing prefecture named after the Huai region, a rich herb-growing area (the 'Four Huai medicines').
candidates.fit: Prefecture seated at Qinyang (Henei county) here; it covered Wuzhi, Wen, Xiuwu, Jiyuan and Mengzhou in regions 12, 18 and 19, but the seat and 70% of this region's people are in it.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article (Huaiqing fu) and Yuan-dynasty route article; 202 hits with Henan, top ones about this prefecture.
candidates.source_note: 治所在今河南省沁阳市，领六县

candidates.name: Qinyang
candidates.meaning: "North of the Qin River": the name since the Republic; before that Henei.
candidates.fit: City holds 38% of the region (98% of the city); the Qin River runs through the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city; always known.
candidates.source_note: 因处沁河之北（阳）而得名

candidates.name: Bo'ai
candidates.meaning: "Universal love": a modern county name (origin not checked).
candidates.fit: County is 32% of the region (99% of the county), but the name is a modern slogan and tells nothing about the place.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: county name

regions.summary: Fengqiu, Yanjin and the east of Yuanyang, Yellow River plain.

candidates.name: Fengqiu
candidates.meaning: "Enfeoffed mound": Liu Bang gave a mound of land to a woman who had fed him when he was in flight, in return.
candidates.fit: 56% of the region's people, 82% of the county; the Fengqiu seat is inside and the Chen Bridge mutiny of 960 is here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; also a Han county for 2000 years.
candidates.source_note: 因汉高祖刘邦为答谢翟母...钦封“丘地”而得名

candidates.name: Yanjin
candidates.meaning: "Extended ford": a Yellow River crossing name (not checked).
candidates.fit: 23% of the region's people, 53% of the county; the county seat lies here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; name known from the Guandu campaign crossings.
candidates.source_note: 延津县 (CHGIS seat 1117-1911)

regions.summary: Yuanyang and Huojia counties, west of Fengqiu.

candidates.name: Yuanyang
candidates.meaning: Name made in 1950 by merging Yuanwu and Yangwu counties.
candidates.fit: 48% of the region's people, 66% of the county; both old county seats were here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, 2000+ years of component counties.
candidates.source_note: 原武、阳武二县合并，定名为原阳县

candidates.name: Huojia
candidates.meaning: "Capture and praise": in 111 BC Han Wudi was brought the head of the Nanyue minister Lu Jia and renamed the township.
candidates.fit: 43% of the region's people, 97% of the county; the county seat and old Huojia of the Han are inside the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 得吕嘉首，以为获嘉县

regions.summary: Jiyuan city, Mengzhou and Jili: the Ji River source on the northern Yellow River bank.

candidates.name: Jiyuan
candidates.meaning: "Source of the Ji": the town at the source of the Ji River, one of the four great ancient rivers.
candidates.fit: 67% of the region's people, 99.8% of the county-level city; holds the Ji Du temple.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city under the province.
candidates.source_note: 济源因济水发源地而得名

candidates.name: Wangwu
candidates.meaning: Wangwu Mountain, the place of the Foolish Old Man who moved mountains, in the Taihang foothills of Jiyuan.
candidates.fit: Mountain lies inside Jiyuan, the region's main unit; also seat of Wangwu county for 600 years.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; 128 hits with Henan, top ones about this mountain.
candidates.source_note: 愚公移山故事就发生在这里

candidates.name: Mengzhou
candidates.meaning: Tang-Song prefecture of Meng (843-1256) on the Yellow River's north bank; meaning of Meng not checked.
candidates.fit: 24% of the region's people, 74% of the city; seat of Mengzhou prefecture 843-1256 is inside.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.

regions.summary: Wuzhi and Wen counties, between the Qin River and the Yellow River.

candidates.name: Wuzhi
candidates.meaning: "King Wu ascended": tradition says King Wu of Zhou climbed here on his way to attack Shang.
candidates.fit: 54% of the region's people, 84% of the county; old Huai county, seat of Henei commandery, is inside.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 相传周武王伐纣路过此地，登高望远，因而得名

candidates.name: Wen
candidates.meaning: Wen, from an ancient river or the hot-spring name, the fief of Su Fensheng after the Zhou conquest.
candidates.fit: 36% of the region's people, 98% of the county; seat of Wen county 221 BC-1911 is inside.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 武王克商，封司寇苏忿生于温

regions.summary: Hua county (75% of people) plus the eastern half of Yanjin, on the Henan plain south of Anyang.

candidates.name: Huaxian
candidates.meaning: County named for the ancient Hua state and the Hua city (Huatai) in the area; one-character county, so -xian.
candidates.fit: Holds 61% of Hua county's people and Hua is 75% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, own zh-wiki article.
candidates.source_note: 滑县为河南省安阳市下辖的一个县

regions.notes: Huixian (a county further north-west) is already labelled on the map; Huaxian looks similar in English but they are different places.

regions.summary: Xinxiang urban core (Hongqi, Muye, Fengquan) plus most of Weihui city.

candidates.name: Xinxiang
candidates.meaning: "New Xiang": from Xinzhong township of Ji county, shortened to Xinxiang (Sui, 586).
candidates.fit: Holds the old centre of Xinxiang city (Hongqi and Muye, over half the people); city rule gives the central region the city name.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture-level city, own zh-wiki article.
candidates.source_note: 《太平寰宇记》：以汲县新中乡简称新乡得名

candidates.name: Weihui
candidates.meaning: "Weizhou splendour": Weihui prefecture/route (Ming-Qing seat at Ji county), city since 1988.
candidates.fit: Weihui is 34% of the people and 56% of the area, holds 72% of the city; but the Xinxiang centre is larger.
candidates.recognisability: County-level city, own zh-wiki article; Weihui prefecture seat for 543 years.
candidates.source_note: 元朝时属卫辉路。明代、清代属卫辉府

regions.notes: Muye (the 1046 BC battlefield) is a district name and also the earlier agents' second idea; it is a fair third option but only a third of the people.
